question: A Canadian home-maintenance note says “clean the eavestroughs.” Which part of the house does that refer to, and what other common word might a neighbour use?
generated_answer:
The term “eavestroughs” is a Canadian English term for what is commonly known as a “gutter” in American English. It refers to the troughs or channels that collect rainwater from the roof and direct it away from the building. The other common word a neighbour might use is “gutters.” The term “eavestroughs” is more commonly used in Canada, while “gutters” is more commonly used in the United States and other English-speaking countries. The task of cleaning the eavestroughs/gutters involves removing leaves, debris, and other obstructions to ensure that rainwater can flow freely and prevent water damage to the building. This maintenance task is typically performed in the fall after the leaves have fallen, and again in the spring to prepare for the new rainy season. It’s important to keep the eavestroughs/gutters clean to prevent water from overflowing and causing damage to the foundation, walls, or basement of the house. In some regions, especially in areas with heavy snowfall, additional maintenance tasks may be necessary to ensure that the eavestroughs/gutters are clear and functioning properly during the winter months. For example, removing snow and ice dams from the roof and eavestroughs/gutters can help prevent water from backing up and causing damage. Regular maintenance of the eavestroughs/gutters is an important part of home maintenance in many parts of the world, and it can help extend the life of the roof and prevent costly repairs. 

In summary, “eavestroughs” refers to the gutters on a house, and a neighbour might use the term “gutters” instead. Cleaning the eavestroughs/gutters is an important home maintenance task that helps prevent water damage and ensures the proper functioning of the roof drainage system. 

If you need help with cleaning your eavestroughs/gutters, you can hire a professional or do it yourself using a ladder, gloves, a trowel or scoop, and a hose or pressure washer. It’s also a good idea to inspect the eavestroughs/gutters for any signs of damage or wear and tear, and to make any necessary repairs to ensure they are functioning properly.
